neighbours.label: The particle or object after 'take' in 'take away' / 'take over' (taking something from someone or assuming it), vs 'take' in other phrasal uses (take a walk, take the bus, take part)
fire: The new rules would take away the farmers' right to sell seeds.
A rival firm plans to take over the struggling airline next year.
Nobody can take away the memories we made that summer.
The city wants to take over the bus routes from the private operator.
The court ruling could take away his license to practice medicine.
If the state takes over the school, the board will be dissolved.
Losing the grant would take away our only source of funding.
The bank agreed to take over the mortgage after the merger.
quiet: The farmers take a break at noon to eat under the trees.
A rival firm plans to take part in the airline auction next year.
We take the ferry to the island every summer.
The city wants to take a closer look at the bus routes.
The doctor told him to take the pills with food.
If the school takes place in a new building, parents will drive farther.
Please take a seat while we prepare the room.
The bank agreed to take notes during the merger talks.

predictions: 'take away'/'take over' items reach 0.4-0.65; other 'take' uses stay under 0.12.
